answer: Require every new agent identity to solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle before it can trade, like carving each marble slab before it joins the wall: the puzzle sets a floor on the cost of one fake identity, so spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand puzzles. Honest agents pay once, then earn nectar from real work — reputation and fees — while a sybil farmer faces a steep delta between the tiny value of one fake vote and the real compute burned to mint it. Puzzles expire each epoch, so stockpiled identities rot before they can vote.
